note: Claims scoped to the TLV62569 (DBV variant): parts, operating limits and the datasheet's layout guidelines. Page numbers are SLVSDG1C's printed pages (sha256 1ba6f55d…). `requirement` gives values in SI-style keys; `checks` the part a board's part values can show (`ccomp check package`); `this_board` entries are the 3.3 V / 600 mA design in schematic/circuit.TLV62569DBV.json, worked from the cited equations. `enforced_by` says which tool does.

claims.statement: VIN is 2.5-5.5 V in operation (6 V absolute maximum); the converter stops below its under-voltage lockout, 2.3 V typical and 2.45 V max with VIN falling, 100 mV hysteresis.
claims.note: The quote is the Recommended Operating Conditions row as pdftotext lays it out. A 1S LiPo (3.0-4.2 V) and USB 5 V are both inside the range.

claims.statement: The output is set by an external divider, VOUT = VFB x (1 + R1/R2) with VFB = 0.6 V (0.588-0.612 V); R2, from FB to ground, is at most 200 kOhm.

citation.quote: When sizing R2, in order to achieve low current consumption and acceptable noise sensitivity, use a maximum of 200 kΩ for R2.

enforced_by: ccomp check package (R2 value; the ratio R1/R2 is not checked)
claims.note: This package's 3.3 V output: R1 = 453k, R2 = 100k, VOUT = 3.318 V nominal (Equation 2).

claims.statement: A 6.8 pF feed-forward capacitor across R1 (VOUT to FB) is recommended with R2 = 100 kOhm, for loop bandwidth and load-transient response; the parts list marks it optional.

citation.quote: 6.8-pF capacitance is recommended for R2 of 100-kΩ resistance.

enforced_by: ccomp check package (CFF value, when R2 is 100k)
claims.note: Valid for R2 = 100 kOhm only; another divider needs CFF rescaled (the datasheet points to SLVA289, which was not read).

claims.statement: L and COUT come from the datasheet's stability matrix: for VOUT >= 1.8 V, 1 uH or 2.2 uH with 10 uF, 22 uF or 2 x 22 uF; 2.2 uH with 10 uF is the standard combination.

citation.quote: Checked cells represent combinations that are proven for stability by simulation and lab test.

enforced_by: ccomp check package (inductance; the L-COUT pairing is not checked)
claims.note: Table 4's columns are 4.7, 10, 22, 2 x 22 and 100 uF; read from the column positions, the 1.8 V <= VOUT row has no 4.7 uF or 100 uF entry. Only the nominal values 1.0 and 2.2 uH are listed; the check admits anything between.

claims.statement: The stability matrix already allows effective inductance +20 %/-30 % and effective output capacitance +20 %/-50 % (tolerance and DC-bias derating), so a part's nominal value is what is checked against it.

citation.quote: Capacitance tolerance and bias voltage de-rating is anticipated. The effective capacitance can vary by +20% and -50%.

claims.note: Refines the library claim: for this chip the -50 % is already inside the table, so a nominal 10 uF that keeps >= 5 uF at 3.3 V is enough.

claims.statement: COUT is a low-ESR ceramic, X5R or X7R, of 10 uF to 47 uF.

citation.quote: The TLV62569 is designed to operate with an output capacitor of 10 µF to 47 µF, as outlined in Table 4.

enforced_by: ccomp check package (capacitance; dielectric is not in a value string)

claims.statement: CIN is a low-ESR multilayer ceramic of at least 4.7 uF; more reduces input ripple.

citation.quote: For most applications, 4.7-μF input capacitance is sufficient; a larger value reduces input voltage ripple.

claims.statement: The inductor's saturation current is 20-30 % above IL,MAX = IOUT,MAX + dIL/2, with dIL = VOUT x (1 - VOUT/VIN) / (L x fSW) and fSW = 1.5 MHz; DCR and size also count.

citation.quote: It is recommended to choose a saturation current for the inductor that is approximately 20% to 30% higher than IL,MAX.

claims.note: Isat is not in a value string, so no check. The high-side current limit (3 A typical on DBV, no min/max given, p.5) bounds the peak in overload; the datasheet does not ask Isat to exceed it. SMNR4020-2.2UH is rated 3.40 A.

claims.statement: This package's inductor, SXN SMNR4020-2.2UH, is 2.2 uH +/-20 % with DCR 0.040 ohm +/-30 % and a rated DC current of 3.40 A max, 4.0 x 4.0 x 2.0 mm, magnetic-resin shielded.

citation.locator: SMNR4020 Series Electrical Characteristics p.4; Shape and Dimensions p.4
citation.figure: Table row SMNR4020-2.2UH: L 2.2 uH, Tol +/-20 %, DCR 0.040 ohm (column header +/-30 %), Rated DC Current 3.40 A Max; dimensions A 4.0, B 4.0, C 2.0 mm; land pattern F 0.95, G 2.1, H 3.3 mm

claims.note: The catalogue does not define 'rated DC current' (saturation or heating); LCSC lists 3.4 A as Isat. Either way it is above this board's 1.04 A requirement and the IC's full-load 2.86 A. Magnetic-resin shielding is not a fully closed molded core.

claims.statement: When VIN approaches VOUT the converter runs at 100 % duty cycle (high-side switch held on) and regulates down to VIN(MIN) = VOUT + IOUT x (RDS(on) + DCR), with RDS(on) of the high-side switch 100 mOhm typical; below that VOUT follows VIN.

citation.quote: In this mode, the high-side MOSFET switch is constantly turned on and the low-side MOSFET is switched off.

claims.note: RDS(on) is typical at VIN = 5 V and 25 °C (no max, no curve against VIN), so the dropout at a 3.4 V cell is an estimate: about 84 mV at 600 mA.

claims.statement: EN is driven or tied, never left floating: high (>= 1.2 V) enables, low (<= 0.4 V) shuts down to 2 uA max.

citation.quote: The EN input must be terminated and should not be left floating.

claims.note: The check fails a board that omits R_EN; such a board must tie the EN port itself (Figure 5 ties EN to VIN). EN input current is not specified.

claims.statement: At light load the converter enters Power Save Mode and the output sits slightly above nominal; a larger COUT reduces this.

citation.quote: In Power Save Mode, the output voltage rises slightly above the nominal output voltage. This effect is minimized by increasing the output capacitor.

claims.statement: CIN, COUT and the inductor are placed as close as possible to the IC, with short, direct and wide power traces for low resistance and parasitic inductance.

citation.quote: The input/output capacitors and the inductor should be placed as close as possible to the IC.

enforced_by: generator objectives w_hot, w_out (once it handles a divider)
claims.note: The datasheet gives no order between them and no number.

claims.statement: The low sides of CIN and COUT connect directly to the power ground beside the IC's GND pin, so the ground potential does not shift between them.

citation.quote: The low side of the input and output capacitors must be connected properly to the power GND to avoid a GND potential shift.

enforced_by: verifier hot_loop_area_mm2, output_loop_area_mm2 (close through the GND pin)
claims.note: Figure 20 puts both capacitors' ground pads on one GND pour a few millimetres apart, against the 10-20 mm separation of buck.ground.cin_cout_separation; not linked as a contradiction because the datasheet states no distance.

claims.statement: The FB sense traces are signal traces kept away from the switch node.

citation.quote: Special care should be taken to avoid noise being induced. Keep these traces away from SW nodes.

claims.note: No distance is given; the intent's 0.3 mm is borrowed from the rp2350 package's floor and is soft.

claims.statement: Ground layers may be used to shield the feedback and other sensitive traces from the power stage.

citation.quote: GND layers might be used for shielding.

enforced_by: verifier feedback_clearance_mm (a plane between counts as shielding)

claims.statement: In TI's DBV layout L1 bridges the SW pin to a VOUT pour above the IC, C1 sits beside VIN and GND, C2 beside SW/GND on the VOUT side, R1 and R2 sit by the FB pin, and the VOUT sense runs from C2 to R1 on another layer.

citation.figure: Figure 20, TLV62569DBV Layout: VIN pour left, VOUT pour right, GND pour below; L1 above the IC, C1 left between VIN and GND, C2 right between VOUT and GND; R2 and R1 below the FB pin; a trace drawn in a second colour, with a via at each end, from beside C2 to R1.

claims.note: The second-layer reading of the sense trace is from its colour and vias; the figure has no layer legend. A template for the generator once it handles SOT-23 pinouts.

claims.statement: The SOT-23-5 package's junction-to-ambient resistance is 188.2 °C/W on the JEDEC board; the junction is rated to 125 °C in operation and shuts down at 150 °C.

citation.figure: Thermal Information table, DBV column: RθJA 188.2 °C/W, RθJB 41.2 °C/W

claims.note: At this board's 600 mA the IC's loss is not given by the datasheet (efficiency curves at 3.3 V out are for VIN = 5 V only, Figure 9); copper on the GND and VIN pins is the heat path.
